content:
MS NOW host Lawrence O’Donnell on Monday ripped Donald Trump over his successful push to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, likening the president’s intervention to a move out of his friend Vladimir Putin’s playbook.

“The most dictatorial president in American history has decided that not only should the American government take partial ownership of American companies, as Donald Trump has done, but also that the president of the United States should decide who the presidents of private companies are,” he said.

“That is Vladimir Putin-style communism.”

Trump — after the company welcomed the tech executive back following his resignation from his post in the wake of alleged affairs with two employees and a suspected Chinese spy — told CNBC he “convinced” the board to bring Huang back and gave it “assurance” that he would not be a threat to national security.

The president — who’s traded tens of millions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia stock during his second term and held as much stock as $62 million at August’s end — told The Wall Street Journal his decision to call up the board over a week ago became “more and more right as the company stock began to tumble.”

“I think they’ll see the result is so positive because the public has spoken today,” said Trump of the stock market surge after the reinstatement Monday.

O’Donnell used his monologue to highlight a piece by The Bulwark’s Jonathan V. Last, who wrote that the U.S. is now a country whose “maximum leader dictates personnel decisions of private companies.”

“We have a word for that sort of thing: communism. It’s what happens in China and Russia. And now it’s what happens here, too,” he wrote.

“We should be very clear about all of this. We should name it and say it out loud. Donald Trump is a communist.”

O’Donnell then played a supercut of Trump using “communist” to attack Democrats at rallies leading up to this year’s midterms.

“Who’s the communist now?” O’Donnell remarked.

Watch more of O’Donnell on MS NOW’s “The Last Word.”
